text:
eloise: Quick dump — ran a small sleight-of-hand prefill probe on the new 13B-quant candidate. wanted to share numbers and a proposed eval plan.

dmitri: Nice, what do you mean by 'sleight-of-hand' here?

eloise: Short: we try a lightweight speculative prefill using a cheap 3B quant model to guess the first N tokens, then confirm with the 13B quant. goal is to trade a tiny quality hit for >2x early-token latency improvement.

ajay: Ah gotcha. So prefill = speculative prefix, but we don't keep final tokens until confirmed? how is fallback handled?

eloise: Exactly. Workflow: 1) run cheap model for tokens 1..K; 2) start streaming those to client while the 13B computes; 3) if 13B disagrees beyond threshold we patch/regen rest. Fallback: if top-prob KL > 0.12 for any token in prefix, abort and re-gen.

sam: Any numbers? microbench or perfbox?

bench-bot: perf snapshot (local dev GPU):
```
model cheap: llama-3-small-3b-quant -> p50 token latency 8ms
model main: ember-13b-4bit -> p50 token latency 22ms
prefill K=6 -> observed client-first-byte p50 ~60ms vs baseline ~140ms
end-to-end p95 improvement ~35% for short prompts
```

dmitri: Those p50s look promising. What about quality delta on E2E benchmarks?

eloise: Ran on a 300-sample holdout (instruction + chat mix):
- exact-match-like metrics: 0.8% drop
- semantic similarity (cosine on embed): mean delta -0.012
- human preference A/B (50 pairs): cheap-prefilled favored 18%, baseline favored 64%, ties 18%

ajay: Hmm human prefs show noticeable regression. Could be prefix instability for tasks needing exact phrases. Any per-task breakdown?

eloise: Yes — summarization and extraction tasks degrade more. Open-ended chit-chat mostly fine. Hypothesis: cheap model frequent tokenization mismatch at entity boundaries.

sam: Can we make cheap model more conservative? e.g., only prefill function words / high-confidence tokens?

eloise: Tried a confidence gate: only prefill tokens with top_proba > 0.6 and gap > 0.25. That reduced regressions to 0.3% but also cut speedups to ~1.5x. tradeoff space.

ajay: What about quantization mismatches? both are quant but different bits. Did you see systematic bias (e.g., shorter completions)?

eloise: Good point. cheap model tends to prefer shorter tail tokens; we added a length-bias correction when merging outputs. still an edge-case when tokens split entities differently.

bench-bot: quick config snippet used:
```
--prefill-k=6 --cheap-model=ember-mini-3b-4bit --confirm-threshold-kl=0.12 --confidence-min=0.6
--length-bias=+0.02
```

dmitri: For a production rollout we need: (A) per-route opt-in, (B) automatic rollback when quality drift > X, (C) telemetry for prefills: prefilled_tokens/confirmed_tokens/regens.

ewoise: Agreed. Proposed eval plan:
1) expanded holdout 5k samples with stratified tasks (QA, extract, summarize, chat).
2) run 3 cfgs: aggressive (K=8, low confidence), balanced (K=6, conf 0.6), conservative (K=3, conf 0.75).
3) collect automatic metrics: BLEU/ROUGE/EM, embed sim, regen rate, token-level KL, latency percentiles.
4) N=500 human judgements per cfg on priority tasks.

ajay: Also add adversarial prefixes that induce entity tokenization splits. We should surface a 'token-split' error category.

eloise: Good call. I'll add a synthetic set that forces byte-pair splits.

sam: What about cost math? If cheap model runs in parallel, we pay both. Do we expect net cost savings?

eloise: Short-run cost goes up slightly (parallel run), but net tokens served from main model drop ~22% on short sessions because many responses complete within prefill horizon. Our estimate: per-short-session cost delta ~ -12% (savings). For long-form sessions cost neutral or worse. So route selection important.

ajay: So product rule: enable for routes where median output length < 40 tokens and high p95 latency sensitivity. Also allow users to opt into 'latency-first' fallback.

eloise: Implementation notes for eng-runtime: need an API flag (prefill: {model, K, conf}) and a short-lived KV to store prefill logits until confirm. We can reuse kv-cache plumbing. Also add tracing span "prefill/confirm" for Console metrics.

sam: Can you post the raw logs and the eval harness config here? I'll start the expanded runs.

eoise: Yep — uploading shortly. For now, here's a quick harness command I used locally:
```
python -m ml_harness.run_prefill --cfg configs/prefill/balanced.yaml --samples 300 --out results/prefill_balanced.json
```

ajay: Great. Once we have expanded results, let's schedule a 30-min sync to decide go/no-go and rollout rules. :calendar: 

eoise: Thanks team. I'll push the configs and a short README to the spec branch. will ping when expanded results are done. :thumbsup:
